content.title: Howard at a Glance | Howard University
content.text: Howard University is one of the nation's leading research universities with a legacy of impact on culture and intellectualism. Howard University, one of the nation's leading research universities, is dedicated to educating students from diverse backgrounds at the undergraduate, graduate and professional levels. Guided by our extraordinary cadre of faculty, students are immersed in cutting-edge scholarship and innovation including nanotechnology, human genome research, atmospheric science, as well as the social sciences, arts and humanities. The only HBCU classified as a top Carnegie-designated research institution.The top HBCU in the nation according to Forbes America's Top Colleges 2024–25Among the nation's top colleges for access and high graduate earnings according to "Opportunity Colleges and Universities - High Access and High Earnings."The most black students earning professional doctorates according to Diverse Issues in Higher Education.The greatest resources for minority students, Princeton Review 2024. No. 86 best colleges in national universities, U.S. News & World Report 2024.Top 12 in the nation for social mobility and no. 1 in the Washington, D.C. area. Howard ranked as the no. 1 HBCU for graduate programs in criminal law, constitutional law, dispute resolution, intellectual property law, health care law, trial advocacy law, economics, English, fine arts, history, political science and speech pathology, according to U.S. News & World Report Best Colleges 2024.Howard ranked as the no. 1 HBCU for undergraduate programs in business, computer science, economics, engineering and psychology, according to U.S. News & World Report Graduate schools in 2025. Howard University School of Law placed no. 13 in law schools with the most graduates at leading law firms, surpassing other institutions with stellar reputations. Most black bachelor's degree graduates in communications and journalism. Academic Programs Students pursue studies in more than 130 areas within the University’s 14 schools and colleges: Arts & Sciences, Business, Communications, Dentistry, Divinity, Education, Engineering, Architecture & Computer Sciences, Graduate School, Law, Medicine, Nursing & Allied Health Sciences, Pharmacy and Social Work. The University offers Master’s Doctoral Professional Joint-Degree and Undergraduate programs.
